messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT INC-20260223-42 created — model alpha4-lite (variant id: alpha4-lite@eu-west-1) p95 latency > 2.5s and error-rate 4.8% on /v1/generate. Affected route: /chat/generate. Triggered by heavy traffic from a small keyset.

maria: paging @kevin and @anya. seeing big tail for alpha4-lite in eu-west-1. dashboards show spikes starting ~09:10 UTC. can we triage impact and decide mitigation?

kevin: on it, joining. attaching quick metric snapshot: `link: internal.metrics.redwood/alpha4-lite/2026-02-23/09:10`

anya: reading traces now. root cause unclear — some memory pressure on older q8 kernels, KV cache misses look high. looks correlated with large batch window from a handful of heavy keys.

maria: immediate mitigation options: 1) soft-disable alpha4-lite routing (steer traffic off, keep variant warm), 2) emergency per-key throttles for heavy keys, 3) fall back to stable-v3 for all new requests. prefer minimal customer impact while stabilizing.

dave: can we do a weighted reduce first? set alpha4-lite weight to 10% and raise stable-v3 to soak 90%? avoids cold-starts.

kevin: agree. do: `rwctl route adjust --model alpha4-lite --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.1 --reason "p95 latency spike"` then `rwctl route adjust --model stable-v3 --region eu-west-1 --weight 0.9`

maria: also please apply emergency per-key quotas for the top offending keys: `rwctl quota set --key KEYID_42 --max-rps 2 --mode emergency` (repeat for list). We should also enable circuit-breaker at 500ms on alpha4-lite to fast-fail high-latency requests.

incident-bot: Runbook step applied: traffic-weight update started (operator: kevin). Exec logs: `deploy-ops-2449.log`

kevin: weights changed, verified via control-plane: alpha4-lite weight=0.1 stable-v3 weight=0.9. watching.

anya: after weight change p95 for alpha4-lite dropped to ~1.4s but stable-v3 p95 rose slightly, still within SLA. KV-cache miss rate still elevated but CPU at nodes reduced. error-rate trending down.

maria: good. notify support to flag any customer-facing errors. @pagerduty please trigger customer impact triage for keys KEYID_42, KEYID_77. potential impact to AcmeCorp and BetaApps.

pagerduty: Pager duty notified. Incident severity set to Sev2. On-call: kevin. Handoff instructions: please post status every 10 minutes until resolution.

kevin: noted. applying per-key throttles now for top 5 keys. commands ran: `rwctl quota set --key KEYID_42 --rps 2`, `rwctl quota set --key KEYID_77 --rps 1` etc.

maria: running a quick smoke: sample requests from AcmeCorp key — responses successful on stable-v3, latencies ~220ms. Good.

dave: can we keep alpha4-lite at 10% for now and let it drain traffic. plan is to promote a rollback to alpha3-compat if tail persists. we should avoid full disable unless we see errors bounce back.

kevin: agree. I'll start an automated canary rollback if alpha4-lite p95 exceeds 2s again for 3 consecutive 1-min windows: `ops-policy set --on-threshold "p95>2s x3" --action "route weight alpha4-lite=0 stable-v3=1"`

anya: adding regression check: tie eval set 'core-sanity' — if quality delta > 1% when rerouted, abort automatic rollback.

maria: for transparency, posting a short blurb to #customer-impact with current mitigation steps and affected customers. keep it factual: we routed most traffic to stable-v3 and applied emergency per-key limits; monitoring for regressions.

kevin: monitoring shows error-rate down to 0.9% and infra metrics stabilizing. alpha4-lite p50 ~120ms, p95 1.2s. still some slow tails for batch sizes >8.

maria: next actions: 1) keep soft routing for 30m and continue throttles, 2) if p95 <1.5s and errors <1% for 30m, we will gradually restore weight to normal. 3) if p95 >2s auto-roll back to stable-v3 fully and open postmortem.

incident-bot: Action logged: emergency throttle + weighted steering. Ticket INC-20260223-42 updated.

anya: FYI I captured kernel stack traces from failing nodes and sent to eng-runtime with label `INC-20260223-42/alpha4-lite`.

kevin: 10min update: metrics continuing to improve. no customer escalations so far.

maria: handing over to @anya for next 2-hour monitoring window. @kevin stay on standby for rollback. I'll update runbook and start incident timeline.

anya: ack — taking lead. I'll post 30min updates and tag eng-runtime if we see recurrence.

pagerduty: Handoff complete. Next oncall: anya. Keep incident channel updated.

kevin: feel free to escalate to full disable if we see error-rate rebound >2% or customer reports. I'll hold the rollback policy until confirmed.

maria: thanks team. quick note for post-incident: consider adding a perf guard for batch sizes >6 on alpha4-lite and a recommendation to prefer stable-v3 for high-concurrency API keys until kernel patch lands.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260223-42 status: Mitigated (soft steering + per-key throttles). Investigation ongoing.

anya: 30min update: stable. moving to monitoring-only. scheduling follow-up with eng-runtime to triage kernel/quantization path.

kevin: closing on-call log. I'll revert emergency quotas when stable for 60min.

maria: thanks all — moving this thread to postmortem once we have root cause. :thumbsup:
